details.title: Agreement for the Provision of Technology Services

governing_law_source.quote: This Agreement and any dispute or claim (including non-contractual disputes or claims) arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales.

details.parties_quote: (1) BRIGHTWATER INSURANCE INC., a corporation organised under the laws of the State of Connecticut, whose principal office is at 185 Asylum Street, 18th Floor, Hartford, Connecticut 06103, United States, a wholly owned subsidiary of Brightwater Group plc (the "Customer"); and (2) ATLIQ INC., a corporation organised under the laws of the State of Delaware (EIN 88-4410273), whose office is at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, New Jersey 08540, United States (the "Supplier").

payment_source.quote: The Customer shall pay correctly rendered and undisputed invoices within forty-five (45) days of receipt.

details.services_summary: Build of claims analytics data mart on Snowflake environment, claims severity and cycle-time dashboards, handover and documentation.

liability_cap.basis: one hundred and fifty per cent (150%) of the Contract Value
liability_cap.quote: Subject to clauses 9, 15.1 and 15.4, the Supplier's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed one hundred and fifty per cent (150%) of the Contract Value.

delay_penalty.quote: If the Supplier fails to achieve any Key Date, the Supplier shall pay to the Customer liquidated damages in the amount of one per cent (1%) of the Contract Value for each day or part day by which the relevant Key Date is missed.

details.one_sided_note: Confidentiality clause 12 binds the Supplier only to keep information confidential, while the Customer is explicitly granted the right to disclose information.

insurance_requirements.quote: The Supplier shall maintain professional indemnity insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000 and cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000.
The Supplier shall maintain professional indemnity insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000 and cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000.

restrictive_covenants.summary: Supplier shall not process Customer Data outside the United States without prior written consent.
restrictive_covenants.restricted_activity: process Customer Data outside the United States
restrictive_covenants.quote: The Supplier shall not process Customer Data outside the United States without the Customer's prior written consent.

findings.title: US entity under non-US law (law of England and Wales)
findings.why: AtliQ Inc has no presence outside the US; disputes would be fought abroad.
findings.comparison: Principle: US law for AtliQ Inc. Brightwater signed this way and it cost $23k.
findings.quote: This Agreement and any dispute or claim (including non-contractual disputes or claims) arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales.

findings.title: Time shall be of the essence
findings.why: Breaching any deadline allows the client to terminate and claim damages immediately.
findings.comparison: AtliQ prefers flexibility and capped delay penalties rather than strict time of the essence.
findings.quote: Time shall be of the essence in respect of the Key Dates.

findings.title: Uncapped daily delay penalties without client-delay exclusion
findings.why: Massive financial exposure; 1% of contract value per day with no cap or delay exclusion.
findings.comparison: Brightwater cost AtliQ previously; principles require capping and excluding client delays.
findings.quote: pay to the Customer liquidated damages in the amount of one per cent (1%) of the Contract Value for each day

findings.title: One-sided indemnity without limitation
findings.why: AtliQ indemnifies Brightwater with no reciprocal protection and no liability cap mentioned here.
findings.comparison: Principles state indemnity should be mutual and proportionate.
findings.quote: The Supplier shall indemnify the Customer and each member of the Brightwater Group against all losses arising from

findings.title: Missing payment for work done on termination
findings.why: AtliQ hands over work in progress without explicitly stating that it must be paid for.
findings.comparison: Principles require AtliQ to be paid for work done on termination.
findings.quote: On termination, the Supplier shall deliver all work in progress and Customer Data to the Customer.

findings.title: No data processing agreement on record for this party in the tracker
findings.why: Personal data needs a signed data processing agreement before it is shared.
findings.comparison: Healthcare deals need an NDA, a BAA and the services contract; European work with personal data needs a DPA.

findings.title: CloudSpan Technologies: Acting as implementation, reseller or referral partner for any competing cloud data-warehouse, lakehouse or analytics platform
findings.why: Exclusivity restricts acting as an implementation partner for competing cloud data-warehouses; Snowflake is mentioned, requiring verification of regional scope.
findings.comparison: Do not partner with another cloud data-warehouse or lakehouse vendor in India or the GCC while the CloudSpan agreement runs.
findings.quote: during the Term Partner and its Affiliates shall not act as an implementation, reseller or referral partner for any Competing Platform in India or the GCC.
findings.exception: Clause 7.3: does not restrict services outside India and the GCC, or to a customer that independently selected a platform, provided AtliQ holds no partner appointment with, and receives no fee from, that platform's provider.

findings.title: Compliance with unprovided Brightwater Group policies
findings.why: AtliQ must comply with policies that are not attached, creating hidden obligations.
findings.comparison: Not standard; creates uncertainty regarding scope and compliance costs.
findings.quote: and the Brightwater Group policies notified to the Supplier

findings.title: Broad right of set-off
findings.why: Allows Brightwater to withhold payments based on disputed claims across the entire corporate group.
findings.comparison: Exceeds standard terms by including group-wide entities in set-offs.
findings.quote: The Customer may set off against any sums owed to the Supplier any amount owed by the Supplier to the Customer or any member of the Brightwater Group.

findings.title: Perpetual and irrevocable license for pre-existing materials
findings.why: Grants permanent rights to AtliQ's proprietary tools beyond what is needed for the deliverables.
findings.comparison: AtliQ usually retains pre-existing tools and licenses them strictly for the deliverables.
findings.quote: grants the Customer and the Brightwater Group a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use any such materials

findings.title: One-sided confidentiality obligation
findings.why: Obligates AtliQ to protect client data but imposes no reciprocal duty on Brightwater.
findings.comparison: Principles require confidentiality to be mutual.
findings.quote: The Supplier shall keep confidential all Customer Data and all information relating to the business

findings.title: High mandatory insurance coverage limits
findings.why: Maintaining USD 2M professional indemnity and USD 1M cyber liability may exceed normal operating costs for this contract size.
findings.comparison: Higher than typical requirements for a USD 92,000 contract value.
findings.quote: The Supplier shall maintain professional indemnity insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000 and cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000.

findings.title: Liability cap is 1.5x annual fee
findings.why: The cap is out of line with the contract value.
findings.comparison: Past contracts: 8 of 10 cap liability at about 1x fees; highest seen 2x.
findings.quote: Subject to clauses 9, 15.1 and 15.4, the Supplier's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed one hundred and fifty per cent (150%) of the Contract Value.

findings.title: Indefinite survival of confidentiality obligations
findings.why: Imposes a permanent burden to protect information without a sunset period.
findings.comparison: Past contracts usually last 6 to 12 months after the term.
findings.quote: This clause 12 shall survive termination indefinitely.

findings.title: Data processing strictly limited to the United States
findings.why: Restricts offshore delivery and remote support flexibility for AtliQ.
findings.comparison: Conflicts with standard global delivery models unless explicitly agreed.
findings.quote: The Supplier shall not process Customer Data outside the United States without the Customer's prior written consent.

findings.title: Asymmetric assignment rights
findings.why: Customer can freely assign within its group, but AtliQ cannot subcontract without prior written consent.
findings.comparison: Creates an asymmetry in operational flexibility.
findings.quote: The Supplier shall not assign or subcontract without the Customer's prior written consent. The Customer may assign this Agreement to any member of the Brightwater Group.
